In [[commutative algebra]], a '''Jaffard ring''' is a type of [[ring (mathematics)|ring]], more general than a [[Noetherian ring]], for which [[Krull dimension]] behaves as expected in polynomial extensions.  They are named for [[Paul Jaffard]] who first studied them in 1960.{{sfnp|Jaffard|1960}}

Formally, a Jaffard ring is a ring ''R'' such that the [[polynomial ring]]

:<math>\dim R[T_1,\ldots,T_n] = n + \dim R, \,</math>

where "dim" denotes Krull dimension. A Jaffard ring that is also an [[integral domain]] is called a '''Jaffard domain'''.

The Jaffard property is satisfied by any Noetherian ring ''R'', and examples of non-Noetherian rings might appear to be quite difficult to find, however they do arise naturally. For example, the ring of [[Algebraic_integer|(all) algebraic integers]], or more generally, any [[Prüfer domain]].{{sfnp|Bouvier|Kabbaj|1988}} Another example is obtained by "pinching" formal [[power series]] at the origin along a subfield of infinite extension degree, such as the subring of <math>\overline{\mathbf{Q}} [[T]]</math> consisting of those [[formal power series]] whose constant term is rational.{{sfnp|Seidenberg|1953}}
